data.narrative:
Senra Systems is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jordan Black and Ben Shanahan, having raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company, with primary focus on three same-stage, same-sector peers: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $112M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $213M. Peer-median analysis of the three comparable robotics companies at Series B yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer method reflects the market positioning of later-stage capital commitments in the sector; the stage-progression method anchors to Senra's actual capital trajectory.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $181M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median implied value of $981M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether Senra's capital efficiency and market traction align with the peer median cohort or track closer to earlier-stage progression norms. Key drivers of final valuation will be revenue scale, customer concentration, and path to capital efficiency relative to the stated peer set.
